[package]
name = "monokl"
version = "0.4.0"
edition.workspace = true
rust-version.workspace = true
license.workspace = true
repository.workspace = true
homepage.workspace = true
authors.workspace = true
categories.workspace = true
keywords = ["monokl", "search", "ast", "typescript", "rust"]
description = "AST-aware semantic code search for TypeScript, JavaScript and Rust."

[lib]
name = "monokl"
path = "src/lib.rs"

[[bin]]
name = "monokl"
path = "src/main.rs"
required-features = ["cli"]

[features]
default = ["cli", "lang-ts", "lang-rust"]

# The TypeScript/JavaScript analyzer, built on OXC.
lang-ts = ["dep:oxc_parser", "dep:oxc_ast", "dep:oxc_ast_visit","dep:oxc_span", "dep:oxc_allocator"]

# The Rust analyzer, built on rust-analyzer's syntax crate.
lang-rust = ["dep:ra_ap_syntax"]

# Agent-facing output via michi, search budgeting, and clap's ValueEnum on CLI-selectable types.
cli = ["dep:clap", "dep:michi", "miette"]

# Miette Diagnostic derive on MonoklError.
miette = ["dep:miette", "michi?/miette"]

[dependencies]
blake3.workspace = true
camino.workspace = true
grep-matcher.workspace = true
grep-regex.workspace = true
grep-searcher.workspace = true
ignore.workspace = true
rayon.workspace = true
regex.workspace = true
rustc-hash.workspace = true
serde.workspace = true
thiserror.workspace = true

clap = { workspace = true, optional = true }
miette = { workspace = true, optional = true }
michi = { workspace = true, optional = true }
oxc_allocator = { workspace = true, optional = true }
oxc_ast = { workspace = true, optional = true }
oxc_ast_visit = { workspace = true, optional = true }
oxc_parser = { workspace = true, optional = true }
oxc_span = { workspace = true, optional = true }
ra_ap_syntax = { workspace = true, optional = true }

[lints]
workspace = true

[dev-dependencies]
peak_alloc.workspace = true
proptest.workspace = true
rstest.workspace = true
serde_json.workspace = true
tempfile.workspace = true
# List available commands
default:
    @just --list

# Install the cargo tools the recipes below use
install-tools:
    cargo install cargo-nextest cargo-llvm-cov cargo-machete cargo-mutants cargo-deny typos-cli zizmor --locked
    rustup component add llvm-tools-preview

# Install the pinned toolchain and the moon-managed git hooks
setup:
    proto install
    moon sync vcs-hooks

# Build the workspace. One `cargo --workspace` invocation, not `moon run :build`: per-crate cargo processes all
# contend for the same target/ lock and serialize.
build:
    cargo build --workspace --locked

build-release:
    cargo build --workspace --release --locked

# Run tests with nextest, plus doctests, which nextest does not run. The default-features pass catches code that only
# builds because --all-features turned something on.
test:
    cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features --locked
    cargo nextest run --workspace --locked
    cargo test --doc --workspace --all-features --locked

# Line coverage; fails below the threshold, which this default owns
coverage threshold="90":
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --all-features --locked --lcov --output-path lcov.info
    cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only --fail-under-lines "{{ threshold }}"

# Coverage report, opened in the browser
coverage-html:
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --all-features --locked --html --open

# Format check, clippy with and without default features, and typos, the same as CI's lint job
lint: typos
    cargo fmt --all --check
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --no-default-features --locked -- -D warnings

# Clippy on the crates moon reports as affected, in one cargo invocation
lint-affected:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    projects=$(moon query projects --affected | jq -r '.projects[].id')
    if [ -z "$projects" ]; then exit 0; fi
    args=()
    for p in $projects; do args+=(-p "$p"); done
    cargo clippy "${args[@]}" --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings

fmt:
    cargo fmt --all

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Compares `monokl search` with ripgrep on pinned public repositories.

monokl is meant to return the few right answers, not everything that matches. So ripgrep supplies the ground truth for
what is right, and the score rewards targeting:

- definitions: files that declare the identifier. The gate is whether one of them is among monokl's first `--top` files
  (hit@top), because an agent that asks for a symbol must be shown where it is declared, early.
- declaration_in_output: whether the declaration's own line appears in monokl's output, so the agent needs no second
  read of the file. Reported, not gated.
- cost: files and output size monokl returns with its default caps, against one `rg -n` call. rg wins on a bare
  identifier, so this is the floor to beat; monokl's case is the question that takes rg several calls.
- test files are left out of the lists, as monokl leaves them out by default. `--tests` also runs monokl with its test
  flag and reports how many test files with the word it returned, ungated.

Questions (scripts/rg-compare.questions) score the case monokl exists for: two to four words that take several rg calls,
with a known answer file and symbol. Each reports the answer file's rank, whether the declaration line is in the output,
the rg route's narrowing cost (files with any word, files with all words, bytes of one `rg -n` call for any word) and
monokl's output bytes. The gate is the answer file in monokl's first `--top` files for at least `--min-question-recall`
of the questions.

Member questions use the same file format with the symbol cell written `member:name`: the answer is a method,
constructor, accessor or arrow-function property declared on an indented line inside a class. The script re-checks that
line with rg and scores them on their own line, apart from the top-level questions. A member question is a hit when the
answer file is in monokl's first `--top` files and the member's declaration line is in the output; the gate is
`--min-member-recall`.

Each repository has a language (the optional fourth column of rg-compare.repos, default `ts`). A `rust` repository is
searched with `*.rs`, its declarations are `fn|struct|enum|trait|type|const|static|mod|macro_rules!` at the start of a
line (optional `pub`, `pub(crate)`), and its members are `fn` and `const` on an indented line inside an `impl` or
`trait` block. `tests/` directories are test files; `#[cfg(test)]` modules are test code for the analyzer, but this
script works on whole files and cannot split them, so a `mod tests` is skipped when sampling and test code inside
source files still counts as source here. monokl runs without `--language`, which searches every registered language,
so no flag is passed. Rust rows (identifiers, questions and members together) are scored apart from the TypeScript
gates and gated by `--min-rust-recall`, which stays 0 until the Rust analyzer ships. A Rust repository that monokl
cannot search yet scores 0 hits, which the report states.

Wall time is reported. Repositories are cloned on demand into target/rg-compare.
"""

import argparse
import json
import re
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
MANIFEST = ROOT / "scripts" / "rg-compare.repos"
QUESTIONS = ROOT / "scripts" / "rg-compare.questions"
CACHE = ROOT / "target" / "rg-compare"
UNCAPPED ="1000000"
# One copy of each rule from `is_test_path` in crates/monokl/src/text_search.rs, which applies every rule to every file.
TEST_DIRS = ("/__tests__/", "/test/", "/tests/", "/spec/")
TS_TEST_SUFFIXES = tuple(
    f".{kind}.{ext}" for kind in ("test", "spec") for ext in ("ts", "tsx", "js", "jsx", "mjs", "cjs", "mts", "cts")
)
RUST_TEST_SUFFIXES = ("/tests.rs", "/test.rs", "_tests.rs", "_test.rs")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Compares `monokl search` with ripgrep on pinned public repositories.

monokl is meant to return the few right answers, not everything that matches. So ripgrep supplies the ground truth for
what is right, and the score rewards targeting:

- definitions: files that declare the identifier. The gate is whether one of them is among monokl's first `--top` files
  (hit@top), because an agent that asks for a symbol must be shown where it is declared, early.
- declaration_in_output: whether the declaration's own line appears in monokl's output, so the agent needs no second
  read of the file. Reported, not gated.
- cost: files and output size monokl returns with its default caps, against one `rg -n` call. rg wins on a bare
  identifier, so this is the floor to beat; monokl's case is the question that takes rg several calls.
- test files are left out of the lists, as monokl leaves them out by default. `--tests` also runs monokl with its test
  flag and reports how many test files with the word it returned, ungated.

Questions (scripts/rg-compare.questions) score the case monokl exists for: two to four words that take several rg calls,
with a known answer file and symbol. Each reports the answer file's rank, whether the declaration line is in the output,
the rg route's narrowing cost (files with any word, files with all words, bytes of one `rg -n` call for any word) and
monokl's output bytes. The gate is the answer file in monokl's first `--top` files for at least `--min-question-recall`
of the questions.

Member questions use the same file format with the symbol cell written `member:name`: the answer is a method,
constructor, accessor or arrow-function property declared on an indented line inside a class. The script re-checks that
line with rg and scores them on their own line, apart from the top-level questions. A member question is a hit when the
answer file is in monokl's first `--top` files and the member's declaration line is in the output; the gate is
`--min-member-recall`.

Each repository has a language (the optional fourth column of rg-compare.repos, default `ts`). A `rust` repository is
searched with `*.rs`, its declarations are `fn|struct|enum|trait|type|const|static|mod|macro_rules!` at the start of a
line (optional `pub`, `pub(crate)`), and its members are `fn` and `const` on an indented line inside an `impl` or
`trait` block. `tests/` directories are test files; `#[cfg(test)]` modules are test code for the analyzer, but this
script works on whole files and cannot split them, so a `mod tests` is skipped when sampling and test code inside
source files still counts as source here. monokl runs without `--language`, which searches every registered language,
so no flag is passed. Rust rows (identifiers, questions and members together) are scored apart from the TypeScript
gates and gated by `--min-rust-recall`, which stays 0 until the Rust analyzer ships. A Rust repository that monokl
cannot search yet scores 0 hits, which the report states.

Wall time is reported. Repositories are cloned on demand into target/rg-compare.
"""

import argparse
import json
import re
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
MANIFEST = ROOT / "scripts" / "rg-compare.repos"
QUESTIONS = ROOT / "scripts" / "rg-compare.questions"
CACHE = ROOT / "target" / "rg-compare"
UNCAPPED ="1000000"
# One copy of each rule from `is_test_path` in crates/monokl/src/text_search.rs, which applies every rule to every file.
TEST_DIRS = ("/__tests__/", "/test/", "/tests/", "/spec/")
TS_TEST_SUFFIXES = tuple(
    f".{kind}.{ext}" for kind in ("test", "spec") for ext in ("ts", "tsx", "js", "jsx", "mjs", "cjs", "mts", "cts")
)
RUST_TEST_SUFFIXES = ("/tests.rs", "/test.rs", "_tests.rs", "_test.rs")

#!/bin/bash
# usage: probe.sh BIN KIND STACK [FILTER] -> max depth that survives (binary search)
BIN=$1; KIND=$2; STACK=$3; FILTER=${4:-probe}
lo=10; hi=2000000
ok() { env KIND=$KIND DEPTH=$1 STACK=$STACK $BIN $FILTER --ignored --nocapture 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^OK'; }
if ! ok $lo; then echo "$KIND fails at 10"; exit; fi
d=$lo
while [ $d -lt $hi ]; do
  n=$((d*2))
  if ok $n; then lo=$n; d=$n; else hi=$n; break; fi
done
while [ $((hi-lo)) -gt $((lo/25+1)) ]; do
  mid=$(((lo+hi)/2))
  if ok $mid; then lo=$mid; else hi=$mid; fi
done
echo "$KIND survives=$lo bytes_per_level=$((STACK/lo))"

    parser.add_argument("--min-rust-recall", type=float, default=0.0,
                        help="fail when the share of Rust hits (identifiers, questions and members pooled) is lower; "
                             "0 until the Rust analyzer ships")
    parser.add_argument("--no-questions", action="store_true", help="skip the question set")
    parser.add_argument("--tests", action="store_true", help="also score test files, ungated")
    parser.add_argument("--json", help="write the full result to this path")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    if not Path(args.binary).exists():
        sys.exit(f"{args.binary} not found; run `cargo build --release` or pass --binary")

    report = []
    for name, url, sha, lang in repositories(args.repo):
        path = checkout(name, url, sha)
        rows = []
        for term in sample_terms(path, args.terms, lang):
            defs, def_tests = split(definitions(term, path, lang), lang)
            seen, seen_tests = split(mentions(term, path, lang), lang)
            (ordered, output), monokl_ms = timed(monokl_files, args.binary, term, path, args.tests)
            monokl_bytes = len(output.encode())
            declaration = declaration_line(term, defs, path, lang)
            # The first 40 characters of the declaration's line, because a signature or snippet may cut a long one.
            # TOON quotes and escapes cells, so compare with quotes and backslashes removed on both sides.
            bare = str.maketrans("", "", '"\\')
            # A signature drops the opening brace, so compare without trailing braces and semicolons.
            # and its export, default and declare keywords.
            wanted = None
            if declaration:
                bare_declaration = re.sub(r"^(?:export\s+|default\s+|declare\s+)+", "", declaration).rstrip(" {;")
                wanted = bare_declaration[:40].translate(bare)
            answered = wanted is not None and wanted in output.translate(bare)
            non_test = [f for f in ordered if not is_test_path(f, lang)]
            found, found_tests = split(ordered, lang)
            _, rg_ms = timed(mentions, term, path, lang)
            rank = first_rank(non_test, defs)
            rows.append(
                {
                    "term": term,
                    "defs": len(defs),
                    "def_rank": rank,
                    "answered": answered,
                    "returned": len(non_test),
                    "rg_files": len(seen | defs),
                    "monokl_bytes": monokl_bytes,
                    "rg_bytes": rg_output_bytes(term, path, lang),
                    "tests": len(seen_tests | def_tests),
                    "tests_hit": len((seen_tests | def_tests) & found_tests),
                    "rg_ms": rg_ms,
                    "monokl_ms": monokl_ms,
                    "top": non_test[:3],
                }
            )

import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

root = Path("/Users/gabe/Projects/monokl/.claude/worktrees/agent-ae68a5da58e663f1b")
old, new = "/tmp/claude/mk/monokl-old", "/tmp/claude/mk/monokl-new"
queries = []
for line in (root / "scripts/rg-compare.questions").read_text().splitlines():
    if not line.strip() or line.startswith("#"):
        continue
    repo, words, _file, symbol = [c.strip() for c in line.split("|")]
    queries.append((repo, words))
    queries.append((repo, symbol.removeprefix("member:")))
extra = [
    ("zod", "parse"), ("zod", "safeParse"), ("zod", "string"), ("zod", "regex:z\\.object"), ("zod", '"object shape"'),
    ("zod", "+union -test"), ("zod", "--exact parse"),
    ("axios", "request"), ("axios", "interceptor"), ("axios", "regex:Promise<"), ("zustand", "create"),
    ("fd", "walk"), ("fd", "regex:fn \\w+"), ("fd", "filter"),
]
queries += extra
seen = set()
unique = []
for q in queries:
    if q not in seen:
        seen.add(q)
        unique.append(q)

diffs = 0
for repo, query in unique:
    path = root / "target/rg-compare" / repo
    args = []
    if query.startswith("--exact "):
        args = ["--exact"]
        query = query.removeprefix("--exact ")
    results = []
    for binary in (old, new):
        proc = subprocess.run([binary, "search", query, str(path), *args], capture_output=True)
        results.append((proc.returncode, proc.stdout, proc.stderr))
    same = results[0] == results[1]
    if not same:
        diffs += 1
        print("DIFF", repo, query, results[0][0], results[1][0], len(results[0][1]), len(results[1][1]))
print(f"{len(unique)} queries, {diffs} differences")
sys.exit(1 if diffs else 0)

Its `parent` is `class Foo` for a class member and `variable api` for the members of `const api = { ... }` (`other default` for `export default { ... }`), and `nodeKind` is `method`, `constructor` or `property`; `parent` is `null` on every other row. A line that matched inside a member is shown on the member's row only, and the class's or object's row appears when it has a match outside its members, such as its name. A first line that says more than the signature stays in, such as a decorator or the start of an arrow function's body. To read the whole block, open the file at `lineStart`–`lineEnd`. 10	
11	/// The stack of the thread that parses and extracts one file, whatever the file.
12	///
13	/// Measured in a build without optimizations, which uses the most: the deepest recursion per nesting unit (see
14	/// `nesting::FRAME_COST`) is 1.7 KB, from a `new` or a generic argument list in TypeScript, and 1.9 KB from a unary
15	/// minus in Rust. The languages' caps are 16,384 and 2,048 units. Every one of the nestings the tests build at the cap,
16	/// 38 in TypeScript and 32 in Rust, parses in 24 MiB and the worst overflows 16 MiB, so 64 MiB is at least 2.6 times
17	/// what the worst accepted file needs. Only the pages a parse touches are committed.
18	pub(crate) const PARSE_STACK_BYTES: usize = 64 << 20;
19	
20	/// Runs `run` on a thread with [`PARSE_STACK_BYTES`] of stack. A panic in it, or a thread that cannot be started,
21	/// yields the [`Degradation`] that says so.
22	///
23	/// A scoped thread per call costs about 20 microseconds against the milliseconds a parse takes, and shares nothing, so
24	/// it keeps the analyzers `Send` and `Sync` without a pool to size.

1	//! A bound on how deep a source file recurses, computed in one pass before any parser or tree walk sees it.
2	//!
3	//! The parsers and the extractors recurse once per nesting level, and a stack overflow aborts the process, so a file's
4	//! depth must be known to be small before it is parsed. [`peak_cost`] estimates the worst recursion the file could cause
5	//! as a number of units, in time and memory proportional to the source length and the limit.
6	//!
7	//! # What a unit is
8	//!
9	//! | Token | Cost |
10	//! | --- | --- |
11	//! | `(` `[` `{` and the `${` of a template | [`FRAME_COST`], and a frame the closer pops |
12	//! | a closer that pops a frame | 1 left behind, because `a()()()` and `a[0][0]` nest through the calls |
13	//! | `<` (generic arguments, JSX, a comparison) | the syntax's angle cost, which `,` does not reset |
14	//! | a word, a number, any other punctuation byte | 1 |
15	//!
16	//! The running cost of a frame is reset to the frame's start at `;`, and to what the frame's angle brackets added at `,`,
17	//! because nothing that recurses survives either. Without semicolons it is also reset when a word starts a new statement:
18	//! after a closing `}`, and after a line that ends in an operand when the next word cannot continue it. A string, a
19	//! comment, a regular expression and the text of a template cost nothing, since no recursion hangs on their content.
20	//!
21	//! # Never an underestimate
22	//!
23	//! An overestimate degrades a file that was not going to be useful. An underestimate lets a hostile file overflow the
24	//! parse stack and abort the process. So wherever the scan cannot tell what a byte is, it takes the reading that costs
25	//! more:
26	//!
27	//! - A closer that does not match the innermost open frame is ignored, and a frame is only ever popped by a closer of its
28	//!   own kind.
29	//! - A quote with no closing quote on its line is an operator, not a string.
30	//! - In a file that may hold JSX, text that looks like a string or a comment may be JSX text, which can hold an
31	//!   expression in braces and nested tags. Such text that contains a `{` is scanned as code, and one that contains `<`
32	//!   charges each of them.
33	//! - A `/` after an operand is a division, so what follows it is code. After a closing `}` it may start a regular
34	//!   expression instead, so the closers up to the next `/` on the line do not pop anything.
35	//!
36	//! Which of these a scan took is observable only in the returned number, so each has a test that a nest hidden behind
37	//! it is still counted.
38	
39	use std::ops::Range;
40	
41	use super::file_analysis::Degradation;
42	
43	/// What a frame costs: a nested bracket is the deepest recursion per byte either parser has, at 1.6 KB of stack per
44	/// level in a build without optimizations. Everything else is priced in this unit; see `PARSE_STACK_BYTES`.
45	pub(crate) const FRAME_COST: usize = 4;
46	
47	/// Which language's lexical rules the scan follows.
48	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
49	pub(crate) enum Syntax {
50	    /// `jsx` is whether the file may hold JSX, whose text can look like strings and comments.
51	    #[cfg(feature = "lang-ts")]
52	    TypeScript { jsx: bool },
53	    #[cfg(feature = "lang-rust")]
54	    Rust,
55	}
56	
57	impl Syntax {
58	    /// The cost of `<`: each level of generic arguments is five tree levels deep in Rust and about three frames' worth of
59	    /// stack in TypeScript, and a comma inside does not end it.
60	    const fn angle_cost(self) -> usize {
61	        match self {
62	            #[cfg(feature = "lang-ts")]
63	            Self::TypeScript { .. } => 2,
64	            #[cfg(feature = "lang-rust")]
65	            Self::Rust => 4,
66	        }
67	    }
68	
69	    /// Whether the source may hold text that is neither code nor a string or comment: JSX text.
70	    const fn text_may_hide_code(self) -> bool {
71	        match self {
72	            #[cfg(feature = "lang-ts")]
73	            Self::TypeScript { jsx } => jsx,
74	            #[cfg(feature = "lang-rust")]
75	            Self::Rust => false,
76	        }
77	    }
78	
79	    /// Whether a word right after a closing `}` on the same line starts a new statement. In JSX it can be the next
80	    /// attribute.
81	    const fn brace_ends_statement(self) -> bool {
82	        !self.text_may_hide_code()
83	    }
84	
85	    /// Whether a line ending in an operand ends the statement when the next line starts with a word. Rust has semicolons.
86	    const fn newline_ends_statement(self) -> bool {
87	        match self {
88	            #[cfg(feature = "lang-ts")]
89	            Self::TypeScript { .. } => true,
90	            #[cfg(feature = "lang-rust")]
91	            Self::Rust => false,
92	        }
93	    }
94	
95	    #[cfg(feature = "lang-rust")]
96	    const fn is_rust(self) -> bool {
97	        match self {
98	            #[cfg(feature = "lang-ts")]
99	            Self::TypeScript { .. } => false,
100	            Self::Rust => true,
101	        }
102	    }
103	}
104	
105	/// The largest cost the source can reach, or the first cost over `limit` if it passes it, which ends the scan early so
106	/// the frame stack stays within `limit / FRAME_COST` entries.
107	pub(crate) fn peak_cost(source: &str, syntax: Syntax, limit: usize) -> usize {
108	    let mut scan = Scan::new(source.as_bytes(), syntax);
109	    while scan.i < scan.bytes.len() && scan.peak <= limit {
110	        scan.step();
111	    }
112	    scan.peak
113	}
114	
115	#[cfg(all(test, feature = "lang-ts", feature = "lang-rust"))]
116	#[path = "nesting_tests.rs"]
117	mod tests;
118	
119	/// `Ok` if `source` nests no deeper than `max_levels` levels of brackets, or the equivalent in other nesting.
120	pub(crate) fn check(source: &str, syntax: Syntax, max_levels: usize) -> Result<(), Degradation> {
121	    let limit = max_levels * FRAME_COST;
122	    let cost = peak_cost(source, syntax, limit);
123	    if cost > limit { Err(Degradation::TooDeep { depth: cost.div_ceil(FRAME_COST), cap: max_levels }) } else { Ok(()) }
124	}
125

132	    cost: usize,
133	    base: usize,
134	    keep: usize,

# 4. Search stays stateless and every stage has a stated bound

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-11-10

## Context

Performance problems kept recurring in different forms:

- The tokenizer vocabulary cost 50 ms on every search with a match. A byte estimate replaced it.
- Dedup was quadratic: 30 ms of 51 ms on broad queries. It is now indexed per file.
- The parallel search kept every file's hits past the file ceiling, so memory was unbounded. It now folds ordered, bounded batches.
- The per-file parse thread sizes its stack by input: 8 MiB + 4 KiB per source byte, capped at 1 GiB for TypeScript and 4 GiB for Rust. Very large generated files return nothing, and a failed reservation degrades output by host.
- `ra_ap_syntax` is quadratic in nesting depth. On a 100 KB file, 20k nested parentheses take 1.06 s and 50k take 4.2 s.
- Nothing has a deadline.
- Memory is bounded by file count, not bytes. 40 files of 5 MB reached 213 MB RSS. One 300 MB line reached 736 MB.
- Text search read every file under the directory, including non-source files, and dropped them afterwards. A path-restricted search over 54,009 files (18,171 of them source) took 2,179 ms against rg's 184 ms. A PR that filters by language before reading fixed it.

Each fix was local. The class of problem was not addressed: a stage whose cost depends on an input property nobody bounded.

## Decision

Search stays stateless: no persistent index, no on-disk cache, no daemon, for now.

Every stage states its bound in its doc comment. Work and memory are bounded by output or by bytes, not by input surprises:

1. No thread stack is sized by input. Parse on a fixed-size stack and reject deep nesting with an O(n) pre-scan.
2. Check file size before reading, and cap hit text length.
3. A global `--timeout` stops analysis early and reports what it skipped in a diagnostic.
4. No step is super-linear in match count. A scaling test in CI asserts the time ratio between two input sizes.
5. Results are deterministic regardless of thread timing: fold in walk order.
6. A file no analyzer owns is never opened.

## Consequences

Stages that violate a rule today are follow-up work, not done:

- Rule 1: the TypeScript and Rust parse threads still size their stack by input, and no nesting pre-scan exists.
- Rule 2: size is not checked before reading, so memory still grows with bytes.
- Rule 3: there is no `--timeout`, so no deadline.
- Rule 4: the per-file dedup fix removed the known quadratic step, but the CI scaling test is follow-up work.
- Rule 5 is what the ordered batch fold already does.
- Rule 6 holds once the language filter before reading merges (PR 79); until then non-source files are still opened.

The trade-off: a stateless search pays the cold cost on every run, and the bounds reject or skip some inputs (deeply nested or oversized files) that analysis would otherwise attempt. Each skip is reported, not silent.

## Alternatives considered

- **Two-phase search.** Score files cheaply from hit counts and path, then analyze only the top 100. Prototyped and rejected. Across 181 queries on three repos, the top-50 rows changed for 20, including rank 1 (`type`, `default`), and 11 changed inside the top 10. On the TypeScript repository, 4 of 30 queries changed at rank 1. Speedups were 1.25x, 0.88x, 0.91x, 1.04x and 1.7x on the 20,000-file set, because text search and the walk dominate (rg alone takes 364 ms there). A safe stopping bound is not cheap to compute: BM25 statistics and the name bonus depend on the whole analyzed set.
- **On-disk analysis cache keyed by content hash.** It helps only warm repeats, and a fresh checkout is cold. It adds writes, invalidation and read-only sandbox problems. Revisit only if warm repeat latency becomes the measured complaint.
- **Long-lived daemon.** A later step, not needed for current numbers. On main, medians on zod and axios are within a few ms of rg, except zod broad queries at 27.7 ms against 18.4 ms, which print 12 KB against rg's 864 KB.

fix: parse files on a fixed stack and reject deep nesting before parsing

The parse thread sized its stack by input, so a file's cost and whether it was analyzed depended on its length and on the host's memory. Every parse now runs on one 64 MiB stack, and a linear scan rejects a file whose nesting could pass it before any parser sees it. The size cap is a measured 4 MiB instead of what a stack could hold, and the post-parse tree-depth check and its leaked trees are gone because no accepted tree is deeper than the drop thread holds.
